title: Do by-elections make Parliament listen?
excerpt: I followed 366 UK by-elections through a century of Hansard. Around polling day the Commons mentions the town 4.0 times as often as similar towns, and a year later still 1.9 times. Before 1945, no detectable rise.
seo_description: When a UK seat holds a by-election, does the Commons talk more about the town? 366 by-elections and a century of Hansard.
header_alt: Title card on cream paper reading 'Do by-elections make Parliament listen?' beside a map of UK by-election towns coloured from blue to red by the change in Commons mentions after the by-election.
